A video cutter online free is the quickest way to cut a video down to the part that actually matters — no app to install, no account to create, and no file uploaded to a stranger's server. Whether it is a long screen recording, a phone clip with dead air at the start, or a video that is simply too long for WhatsApp, you can open the cutter in your browser, pick your start and end points, and download a clean MP4 in a couple of minutes.

![Video editing timeline with clips and a playhead on a computer screen](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1574717024653-61fd2cf4d44d?w=1200&q=80)

## How to cut a video online free in 3 steps

The whole job takes three steps, and you can do it on a phone or a computer — the cutter runs entirely in your browser tab.

### Step 1: Open the cutter and add your video

Open the [free video cutter](/tools/video-trimmer) and drop in your clip. It accepts MP4, WebM, and MOV files up to about 100 MB. The video opens in a preview player right in the browser — nothing is uploaded anywhere, so a private recording stays private.

### Step 2: Set your start and end points

Scrub through the preview to find where your clip should begin and end. You can type the start and end times in seconds — to a tenth of a second, so 12.5 means twelve and a half seconds in — or pause the video at the exact frame and press "Use current ▶ start/end" to set the point from the playback position. Take a moment here: a cut that starts half a second too late can lose the first word of a sentence.

### Step 3: Export and download your MP4

Press "Trim & export MP4", preview the result, and download the clip. The export is an MP4 (H.264 video with AAC audio) with faststart enabled — the most compatible combination there is, so it plays on phones, in browsers, on TVs, and in almost every editor without conversion.

## Why cut video in the browser instead of an app?

Most video editors can cut a clip, but they usually ask for something first: an install, an account, or an upload of your footage. A browser cutter asks for none of that.

- **No install, no sign-up.** It works on any computer or phone with a browser. Borrowed laptop, library PC, a friend's phone — the tool is the same everywhere.
- **No upload.** The cutting runs locally with ffmpeg.wasm inside your browser tab, so your video never touches a server. That matters for screen recordings with passwords on screen, family clips, and work footage.
- **No watermark.** Many popular online cutters stamp a watermark on free exports or lock the clean export behind a paid plan. This cutter adds none — the file you download is the file you cut.
- **Frame-accurate cuts.** The clip is re-encoded rather than cut on the nearest keyframe, so the cut lands exactly where you set it — not a second early or late the way quick-cut tools do it.

## Cut video for WhatsApp, Reels and Shorts

Most of the time you are cutting for somewhere specific: a WhatsApp status, an Instagram Reel, a YouTube Short, or a clip to send in a group chat. A couple of habits make those cuts much better.

### Keep the best moment, cut the rest

Watch the clip once and note the exact moment the good part starts — the punchline, the goal, the reaction. Then set your start point a beat before it, not on it, so the viewer gets a split second of context. Cut the outro the same way: end the clip just after the payoff, not ten seconds into the awkward silence that follows.

### Shorter usually performs better

A tight 30-second clip gets watched to the end far more often than a rambling two-minute one. If you are unsure where to cut, trim a 10-second sample first and test it — it confirms the workflow on your device and shows you how the finished clip will look before you commit to cutting a long recording.

## Video cutter vs video trimmer: is there a difference?

They are the same job with two names. "Video cutter" is the phrase most people type into Google; "video trimmer" is what the tool itself is called. Both mean removing the unwanted start and end of a clip and keeping the middle.

One word that does mean something different is "splitter": splitting cuts a video into several separate pieces. This cutter exports one continuous clip between your start and end points — if you need two separate clips from one video, run it twice with different start and end times.

## The honest limits

A free browser cutter handles everyday clips easily, but it has real limits worth knowing before you start:

- **One continuous clip.** To remove a middle section, export the two halves separately — most free editors can join them in seconds. The cutter cannot delete the middle and join the rest in one pass.
- **File size.** Videos up to about 100 MB work. If your file is bigger, shrink it first with the [free video compressor](/tools/video-compressor), or convert an unsupported format with the [video converter](/tools/video-converter) — it turns MOV, MKV, WebM, and AVI into MP4.
- **Speed.** Because the clip is re-encoded for frame accuracy, export takes time. A few minutes of footage is comfortable; an hour-long recording will be slow on most devices, so trim long recordings on a desktop or laptop rather than a phone.
- **Quality.** Re-encoding always costs a tiny amount of quality, but at the settings used here the difference is invisible for normal viewing — and the output plays everywhere, which is the trade-off that matters.

## Troubleshooting: when a cut doesn't work

- **The export is slow or the tab feels stuck.** Long files take a while because they are re-encoded. Close other tabs to free up memory and let it finish — or cut the recording into shorter pieces first.
- **Your file won't open.** Check the format: the cutter accepts MP4, WebM, and MOV. MKV and AVI files need converting first — run them through the [video converter](/tools/video-converter) and then cut the MP4.
- **The cut landed a fraction off.** Re-check your times. The cutter works to a tenth of a second, so pause at the exact frame and use the "Use current ▶ start/end" button instead of guessing the time.
- **No download appears on iPhone.** Check the Files app under Downloads, and allow the download if Safari asks. Avoid Private Browsing, which blocks downloads entirely.

## Cut your first clip now

Cutting a video should not need an app install, an account, or a paid plan — and it should not stamp a watermark on your work either. Open the [free video cutter](/tools/video-trimmer), drop in your clip, and keep only the part worth watching.
